extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties in AIA/PTAB proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, counsel), PTAB judges and staff
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and application of proposed and existing PTAB (AIA) procedural rules governing petitions, briefing, discovery, confidentiality, panels, and other trial practice matters before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protections (motions to seal and protective orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may seek protection of truly sensitive information from public disclosure by filing motions to seal and proposed protective orders; Rule 42.54 provides for protective orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 42.14 provides that information subject to a motion to seal is provisionally sealed on receipt of the motion pending the decision. Under Rule 42.54 the Board may issue orders to protect parties/persons from disclosing confidential information, including forbidding disclosure or discovery. Rule 42.56 provides for expungement of improperly filed confidential information. The Office will revise the protective order in the Office Trial Practice Guide to place the burden on the designating party to show good cause for sealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early discussion of discovery and protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are encouraged to discuss discovery matters, including confidentiality and whether a protective order is necessary, early in proceedings to resolve disputes before they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic entry of a protective order in every proceeding is not necessary; default protective order (Office Trial Practice Guide Appendix B) exists but parties may propose stipulated protective orders. Purpose of default order is to encourage prompt agreement and avoid lengthy disputes that undermine efficient, less costly alternative to litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of word counts for key briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt word counts (instead of page limits) for the petition, preliminary response, patent owner response, and petitioner's reply brief; retain page limits for other briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching to word counts gains administrative efficiencies (petitions won’t be reviewed to determine whether claim charts contain argument), streamlines administrative review, and reduces non-compliant petitions requiring correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of petition page/word limits (not tied solely to number of claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition length should not be determined solely by number of claims challenged nor by automatic extensions tied to excess claim fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board declined to adopt claim-count-based limits because Rule 42.22(a) requires presentation of precise relief, significance of evidence, material facts, governing law, and substantive unpatentability discussion; word limits for inter partes review, CBM, and post-grant review are expected to be sufficient, with waiver available under 37 CFR 42.24(a)(2) in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted contents and limits on claim charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts must not be used to present attorney argument, claim construction, or to bootstrap arguments/evidence to circumvent page/word limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board FAQ D12: placing argument or claim construction in claim charts to circumvent formatting/page limits is not permitted and any such material may not be considered. Claim charts previously accepted with argumentative content were due to initial unfamiliarity; correction is now required when petition includes improper use of claim charts. With word counts, parties could nonetheless attempt to include argument in claim charts — improper usage remains prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief at preliminary stage (petitioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner's reply at the preliminary (pre-institution) stage is not available as of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office declines to adopt a reply as of right at the preliminary stage because it would introduce additional arguments that are not in the petition and increase review burden. The Board will continue to consider requests for permission to file reply briefs on a case-by-case basis (e.g., to respond to testimonial evidence submitted by a patent owner in the preliminary response). Proposed rules include an explicit provision affording opportunity to seek permission to file a reply responding to testimonial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner reply length and surreply policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner's reply to patent owner response page limit increased to 25 pages; surreplies are not adopted and replies raising new issues or belated evidence will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office adopted increased page limit for petitioner's reply to 25 pages. The Patent Trial Practice Guide provides that replies raising new issues or belated evidence may be returned and not considered; therefore a surreply is unnecessary to address new issues in a reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement discussions (encouraged, not mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement discussions are encouraged but should not be mandatory or disrupt statutory timelines; Board involvement is determined case-by-case and termination following settlement is discretionary under Rule 42.74.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office often includes meet-and-confer requirement in Scheduling Orders. Rule 42.74 gives Board discretion to determine unpatentability after settlement; this provides flexibility to balance public interest in resolving unpatentability issues with efficient allocation of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of precedential and informative decisions (SOP 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: SOP 2 governs recommendation and designation of opinions as precedential or informative: any Board member may recommend designation; parties/public may request designation within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office declined to adopt a rule-based designation process; SOP 2 (Rev. 9) provides sufficient guidance and engages stakeholders. The Board also posts representative orders/decisions (not precedential/informative) that guide recurring issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic revisions to the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will revise and periodically update the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revised Guide will be published with final rulemaking and updates will be issued as needed in the future to reflect practice and rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing system integration and publication of decisions/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements to PRPS and integration with PAIR, plus continued posting of final written decisions and availability of AIA statistics, are considered but no changes to data availability were adopted at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final written decisions are uploaded into PAIR after issuance, and all final Board decisions are posted on eFOIA. Office is working with vendors to improve PRPS functionality (searching, UI) and maintain archived statistics at PTAB statistics page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial institution of grounds (institution on some grounds only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may institute on some but not all grounds presented in a petition (partial institution) to manage workload and meet statutory time constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial institution balances fairness with finite trial timeframe; Office is mindful of ramifications when grounds are in different statutory classes or when references can be sworne-behind and will continue to assess whether balance is appropriately struck.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of estoppel under 37 CFR 42.73(d)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel precludes an applicant/owner from obtaining a claim that is not patentably distinct from a finally refused or canceled claim in an AIA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office declined to change the rule; the rule appropriately prevents seeking claims not patentably distinct from finally refused/cancelled claims. Clarification that estoppel does not arise where an amendment is proposed but not granted was requested, but no rule change was proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition, potential pilot for single-APJ institution, and expanded panels (SOP 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about bias from same APJs deciding institution and trial; Office may pilot single-APJ decision on institution with two additional APJs assigned if trial instituted; SOP1 describes expanded-panel situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office believes panels are unbiased but is exploring efficiency/ fairness via a separate Request for Comments on a pilot under which a single APJ determines institution and two additional APJs join if a trial is instituted. SOP1 (Rev. 14) describes reasons for using expanded panels; requests for rehearing may identify matters the Board misapprehended/overlooked and do not necessarily require identification of conflicting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing requests content and standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing should identify matters the moving party believes the Board misapprehended or overlooked and where each matter was previously addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 42.71(d) requires a moving party to identify all matters believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked and the place where each matter was previously addressed; rehearing is an opportunity to address such issues and may include identification of conflicting Board or court decisions but does not necessitate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and management of interlocutory motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Scheduling Orders allow stipulation to adjust most deadlines; Office will not require resolution of interlocutory motions at particular points but parties may bring motions warranting early attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Scheduling Order allows parties to stipulate to adjust deadlines for patent owner response, petitioner reply, briefing on motions to amend, and motions to exclude (except certain reply briefs). If parties cannot agree on dates, they are encouraged to contact the Office. Office remains open to early attention if a motion would truncate the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and persuasion language (37 CFR 42.20(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed change to explicitly refer to both burden of proof and persuasion and to place burden on 'petitioning or moving' party was declined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office appreciated the comment but declined to amend the rule; existing language remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: APJ training and technological invention standard (37 CFR 42.301(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about need for additional training (e.g., payments industry) and suggested amendment to 37 CFR 42.301(b) were considered; Office declines to amend 42.301(b) as written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office continues to assess training needs for employees; 42.301(b) properly reflects the standard for determining 'technological invention' and will not be amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior claim constructions (issue preclusion not adopted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office will consider prior claim constructions from other proceedings but will not apply strict issue preclusion; claim construction will be decided case-by-case given different approaches and evidentiary records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PTAB may follow a different claim construction approach than district courts and evidence may differ, strict issue preclusion is inappropriate in every case; determinations will depend on facts presented in the particular proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition practice (notice timing, scope objections, costs, conferring with witness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 42.53(d)(4) requiring filing a notice of deposition at least 10 days before may be restrictive; clarification requested on when counsel may object as beyond scope, who bears costs of witness testimony, and conferring with witnesses during depositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office invites comments on whether to amend 42.53(d)(4) to reduce lead time or allow stipulation. Scope objections are best handled case-by-case. Guidance on witness expenses is in the Patent Trial Practice Guide (77 FR at 48761). Office believes Practice Guide strikes the correct balance on conferring with witnesses but invites further comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to serve evidence inconsistent with a party's position (authentication/public availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner advancing that a reference is not authentic or not publicly available has an obligation to serve relevant information inconsistent with its position concurrent with any objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 42.51(b)(1)(iii) requires parties to serve relevant inconsistent information concurrent with the filing of the documents or things that contains the inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backup counsel filing permissions and electronic service (37 CFR 42.6(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may identify one backup counsel with the same filing permissions as lead counsel; additional backup counsel may be identified but only lead counsel and the first backup may file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office is improving electronic filing and case management. Service by email under § 42.6(e) should remain optional upon agreement of the parties to accommodate users who do not use email or prefer mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to sanction misconduct and Rule 11-type certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Office has authority to sanction improper conduct (37 CFR 42.12) and proposes adding a Rule-11 type certification for all papers filed with the Board with sanctions for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposed certification would apply to practitioners and parties. Office declines to amend 37 CFR 42.65(a) to require that unsupported expert reports be entitled to 'no weight', but sanctions authority addresses improper authorship or misconduct regarding expert reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring fairness and responsive rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Office continues to monitor fairness of AIA proceedings and to engage stakeholders (e.g., via notice-and-comment) to ensure proceedings are efficient and fair under congressional mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of responsive changes include Quick-Fix rulemaking (additional pages for certain briefing, claims appendix), guidance on motions to amend (MasterImage 3D decision), proposed word count adoption, and proposed Rule-11 type certification to police practitioner conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of second petitioners/joinder and declining institution for duplicative grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Office has discretion under 35 U.S.C. 314(a), 315(d), 324(a), 325(d) to decline to institute where same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented; Office will not assign a 'junior party' role or terminate proceedings merely because an original petitioner settles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office strives for consistency but declines to adopt automatic junior-party status or termination if earlier parties settle; each party is entitled to assert its interest and the Office may decline institution where duplicative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of material facts option retained (37 CFR 42.22 and 42.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: The option to file a proposed statement of material facts is retained and any such statement is included in page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office declines to eliminate the option despite infrequent use and panel differences about whether such statements count in page limits; see 37 CFR 42.24 for inclusion details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and timing of demonstrative exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about demonstratives (timing for exchange, whether argument may be used with citation, striking demonstratives) exist; disputes are best handled on a case-by-case basis with the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office prefers resolving demonstrative exhibit disputes in the context of the specific case with the assigned panel rather than by bright-line national rule; parties may seek timing that allows objections and resolution before oral hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public outreach and interactive programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will continue outreach (Board-side chats, road shows, lunch-and-learn programs, webinars) to gather input and improve fairness and effectiveness of AIA proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interactive programs are considered valuable input and the Office adopted the comment encouraging continued outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response: optional but may present new testimonial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner preliminary response remains optional under 35 U.S.C. 313, but proposed rules allow patent owners to present new testimonial evidence with the preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing testimonial evidence at the preliminary stage may encourage patent owners to participate early and address petition issues; the Office declines to make filing a preliminary response mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of Practice Guide guidance into rules and pro hac vice criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestion to incorporate guidance in the Patent Trial Practice Guide (and pro hac vice criteria reflected in case law) into formal rules was raised; Office response indicates continued consideration and revision of the Practice Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office is working on revising the Practice Guide and expects future updates; no direct rule changes adopting Practice Guide guidance were made in this notice, but the Office may consider such incorporations in the future.
